listing.name: Baldur's Gate II (original) (GemRB)
listing.summary: Set up Baldur's Gate II (original) through its upstream gemrb player using your own original files. Setup, profiles and updates stay upstream-owned.
listing.original_game_title: Baldur’s Gate II: Shadows of Amn

steps.title: Use this original game and edition
steps.instruction: Use a complete installed original Baldur’s Gate II: Shadows of Amn working copy, with Throne of Bhaal only if you own and installed it. Enhanced Edition files and the trivial demo do not supply the original edition. Keep your originals elsewhere unchanged; upstream handles its own data recognition and preparation. A Portcove registration does not authenticate original-game files.

steps.title: Prepare upstream and select the real player
steps.instruction: For Windows x64, use the official SourceForge archive with its plugins, scripts and configuration. Its v0.9.5 ZIP is named gemrb-win32-v0.9.5.zip and contains a 64-bit player. The player needs the Microsoft Visual C++ x64 runtime. Give this game its own configuration: GamePath points to a separate complete working copy of the installed original; GameType=bg2. Use the configuration supplied with your actual build rather than leaving @...@ development-template placeholders. Register gemrb.exe with the complete GemRB installation as working directory and two literal argument lines, -c then the absolute path to this game’s configuration.

steps.title: Keep the actual original and player data
steps.instruction: Choose a dedicated empty private CachePath for this game: GemRB clears that directory, so it must never be your originals, saves or profile root. SavePath is the parent containing save/, not save/ itself. Keep a separate SavePath per game.

steps.title: Choose the upstream Linux build
steps.instruction: Use the official x86-64 GemRB AppImage with the host libjack.so.0 library, or install org.gemrb.gemrb from Flathub on x86-64 or ARM64 Linux. Start the Flatpak normally once to create GemRB.cfg in ~/.var/app/org.gemrb.gemrb/config/gemrb. For that package, copy this title’s complete original working copy to ~/.var/app/org.gemrb.gemrb/data/baldurs-gate-2, and use that absolute GamePath in a separate baldurs-gate-2.cfg. Use a writable SavePath parent and an empty, dedicated CachePath under the same app’s data and cache directories. Start with flatpak run --command=gemrb org.gemrb.gemrb -c followed by the absolute config path in quotes. This passes the path to the player as one argument. Back up the sandbox config and actual saves separately. To register the standalone x86-64 AppImage, allow the downloaded file to run and select the AppImage itself in Portcove. Choose your private working folder. Enter -c and the absolute path to this game’s config on separate argument lines, then review and save the selection. If the official AppImage reports that it cannot mount, add --appimage-extract-and-run as the first separate argument. Keep -c and the config path on their own lines. Play starts the upstream player. For Flatpak, use the command above.

steps.title: Choose the upstream Mac build
steps.instruction: Use the Mac Source Ports Universal 2 DMG at https://github.com/MacSourcePorts/MSPBuildSystem/releases/tag/GemRB_0.9.5. Its v0.9.5 build uses macOS 10.15 or later on Intel and macOS 11 or later on Apple Silicon. GemRB’s SourceForge release directory also offers separate Intel and Apple Silicon builds. Keep the bundle complete. Use this game’s own configuration and point GamePath to the prepared original game folder. Keep this title’s saves, config and working data together when replacing the bundle. To register the Mac Source Ports bundle, copy the complete gemrb.app from the DMG and open it normally once. Select gemrb.app/Contents/MacOS/gemrb in Portcove. Choose your private working folder, then enter -c and the absolute path to this game’s config on separate argument lines. Review the selection and choose Play.

steps.title: Add the game and manage your files
steps.instruction: Finish setup with the project’s tools before adding the game. Portcove saves your selected executable, working folder and launch arguments; choose Play separately when you are ready. You manage this game’s files, original files and profile. Removing its registration leaves those files in place. Portcove does not offer updates, backups, rollback, data migration or file deletion for this external copy. Keep a working copy and its data before changing versions. Other platforms need their own supported application and setup instructions.

warnings: GemRB clears its cache directory. Use a dedicated private CachePath, separate from original files, saves and profile roots.

GemRB can also write gem-*.ini into GamePath before trying SavePath, so preserve and use a working data copy; SavePath alone does not isolate original installation writes. Preserve that working copy, actual save/config locations and mods with GemRB closed before updates. Do not move saves between different games or editions.
These sibling routes use upstream setup, launch and replacement. Keep the creating runtime and actual player files recoverable before changing versions.

presentation.manual_preparation: Use a complete installed original Baldur’s Gate II: Shadows of Amn working copy, with Throne of Bhaal only if you own and installed it. Enhanced Edition files and the trivial demo do not supply the original edition. Keep your originals elsewhere unchanged; upstream handles its own data recognition and preparation. A Portcove registration does not authenticate original-game files. Use a complete upstream GemRB build with its plugins, scripts and supplied configuration, not just a loose executable. Use the configuration supplied with your actual build rather than leaving @...@ development-template placeholders. Register gemrb.exe with the complete GemRB installation as working directory and two literal argument lines, -c then the absolute path to this game’s configuration. Choose a dedicated empty private CachePath for this game: GemRB clears that directory, so it must never be your originals, saves or profile root. SavePath is the parent containing save/, not save/ itself. Keep a separate SavePath per game. GemRB can also write gem-*.ini into GamePath before trying SavePath, so preserve and use a working data copy; SavePath alone does not isolate original installation writes. Preserve that working copy, actual save/config locations and mods with GemRB closed before updates. Do not move saves between different games or editions. Finish upstream setup first. Registration saves your selected executable, working directory and literal arguments; Play is a separate explicit action. You and upstream own this external runtime, original files and profile. Registration-only removal preserves them. Managed Update, Backup, Rollback, migration and deletion are not offered for these external files. If the AppImage cannot mount, add --appimage-extract-and-run before -c. On Intel or Apple Silicon Mac select gemrb.app/Contents/MacOS/gemrb from the intact Mac Source Ports bundle.
